Egyptian Court Orders Closure of Independent News Outlet Mada Masr and Fines Editor-in-Chief

29 Oct 2026, 01:30 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.nbcnews.com

Image: www.nbcnews.com — Creative Commons

Key takeawaysAn Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of the country's last remaining independent news outlets, following the conviction of its editor-in-chief and founder, Lina Attalah. The court ruled on charges of operating a website without a license, marking

An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of the country's last remaining independent news outlets, following the conviction of its editor-in-chief and founder, Lina Attalah. The court ruled on charges of operating a website without a license, marking a significant development in Egypt's press landscape.

Verdict and Legal Proceedings

During the session at a Cairo misdemeanor court, the presiding judge rejected procedural requests made by the defense and directed lawyers to immediately deliver closing arguments, according to Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, who attended the hearing. When Attalah's defense team of eight lawyers refused, the judge appointed an unknown court-appointed lawyer over the objections of the defense and Attalah.

Following the verdict, Attalah was released after paying a fine equivalent to about $53,400. Mada Masr reported that she had been detained for seven hours following the ruling, with her whereabouts unknown during that period. While completing release paperwork, her legal team learned she had also been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of spreading false news and operating an unlicensed website—a conviction her team intends to challenge.

Background and Context

Mada Masr has long operated under severe restrictions; Egyptian authorities have blocked its website domestically since 2017. The outlet stated it initially applied for an official license in 2018 but never received a response. The publication is known for investigating government corruption, human rights violations, and the expanding role of the Egyptian military in a media environment where most television stations and newspapers are tightly controlled by authorities.

International organizations and local unions have strongly criticized the ruling. Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch condemned the action as a severe blow to press freedom. Khaled Elbalshy, head of the Egyptian Journalists Syndicate, called the verdict a wake-up call that runs counter to demands for media reform.

The case unfolds amid a wider crackdown on independent journalism in Egypt. On the same day as the ruling, prosecutors extended the pre-trial detention of six journalists from the Matsadaash investigative platform by 15 days. Those reporters were arrested in late September on charges including joining a terrorist group and spreading false information.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers and observers analyzing the situation can evaluate the confirmed facts and remaining uncertainties based on available statements from legal representatives, rights groups, and press organizations:

  • What is confirmed: An Egyptian court ordered the closure of Mada Masr and fined editor-in-chief Lina Attalah, who was released after paying the penalty. Attalah's defense team plans to appeal the closure order and a separate 2024 in-absentia sentence. Mada Masr's website has been blocked in Egypt since 2017, and the outlet states it has awaited a licensing response since 2018.
  • What remains uncertain: The ultimate outcome of the planned appeals and the future operational status of Mada Masr's staff remain to be determined by upcoming court dates, including an appeal hearing scheduled for Nov 11.
  • How to verify: Readers can review the original reporting and official statements directly through the primary coverage published by [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-east/court-orders-closure-one-egypts-last-independent-media-outlets-rcna606065).
